title: multi-gpu-serving-design-tensor-pipeline-nccl-sharding-draft
content:
Purpose
-------
This is a working draft for multi-GPU serving design focused on combining tensor/pipeline parallelism, NCCL tuning, and sharding strategies, plus KV cache semantics across devices. The immediate goal is to distill concrete design decisions and a prioritized experiment plan so we can validate performance and reliability targets for Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.

Status
------
- Draft: architecture options explored, initial implementation notes and perf tuning checklist.
- Target: land an MVP implementation (tensor+pipeline support + basic NCCL tuning) and run scale experiments (up to 8 GPUs) by end of Q1.

Goals
-----
1) Serve large transformer models (7B->70B) with predictable latency and high throughput.
2) Support a hybrid of tensor parallelism (TP) + pipeline parallelism (PP) for models that exceed single-GPU memory or compute.
3) Ensure KV cache semantics remain correct and performant across sharded states.
4) Provide templates/configs for NCCL tuning across common infra topologies (DGX-style NVLink, cloud VPCs with EFA/GPUDirect, and multi-host over RDMA).
5) Keep fallback paths to smaller model variants or non-sharded execution when failures occur.

Constraints and assumptions
-----------------------
- Target hardware: NVIDIA A10/A100/H100 class GPUs.
- Networking: we expect both single-host NVLink rings and multi-host RDMA; must support both with sensible defaults.
- Models: standard decoder-only and encoder-decoder transformers (causal generation is priority).
- We prioritize inference (single-token step latency for streaming) over throughput-only batch workloads, but must expose knobs to shift between objectives.

High-level approach
-------------------
- Combine TP for large-matrix shards (weight sharding across GPUs for compute/memory scaling) with PP for extremely deep models (partition layers into pipeline stages).
- Use NCCL backend for inter-GPU collectives (all-reduce, reduce-scatter, all-gather) and fallback to TCP when NCCL not available.
- Maintain a distributed KV cache with explicit sharding mapping to the TP layout to avoid cross-device broadcast for every step.
- Scheduling: runtime will be aware of model placement (TP/PP layout) and will try to co-locate requests with hot KV shards, prioritize low-latency tails with preemption-like fast-paths.

Architecture details
--------------------
1) Placement abstractions
   - Logical shards: model weights are partitioned into "tensor shards" (for TP) and "pipeline stages" (for PP). Each logical shard maps to one or more physical GPUs.
   - Placement descriptor: small JSON/YAML that describes mapping: {stage_id -> gpu_list, tp_degree -> N, shard_map -> [...]} (we will persist as flat text metadata in model bundle).

2) Tensor parallelism (TP)
   - Strategy: row/column partitioning of large matmuls (follow Megatron/DeepSpeed style). Use reduce-scatter + local compute + all-gather for outputs as needed.
   - Ops impacted: Large FC layers, attention projections (QKV, out_proj).
   - Implementation notes: prefer NCCL reduce-scatter/all-gather primitives to minimize peak memory; where possible use fused kernels that accept sharded inputs.

3) Pipeline parallelism (PP)
   - Strategy: split layers into pipeline stages (micro-batching for bubble hiding). For inference, we aim for streaming-friendly PP with small micro-batch sizes and minimal pipeline bubbles.
   - Control flow: adopt one of two modes: synchronous PP (simpler, predictable latency) or asynchronous streaming PP (higher throughput, more complex backpressure). MVP: start with synchronous PP with 1-2 micro-batches.

4) Mixed TP+PP considerations
   - Coordination: each pipeline stage may itself be TP across multiple GPUs. Communication patterns: intra-stage collectives (TP) and inter-stage point-to-point activations (PP).
   - Activation sharding: avoid full activation all-gathers when possible - keep activations partitioned to match TP shard layout, reducing inter-stage bandwidth.

5) KV cache design across shards
   - KV placement: key/value tensors are sharded consistent with tensor-parallel weights so that each GPU owns the KV for its parameter shards.
   - Read path: at generation step t, the GPU that owns the relevant shard performs local attention compute; cross-shard reduce happens only when required for final logits (or for cross-attention merges in encoder-decoder models).
   - Write/evict semantics: append-only per-request until request completes. Eviction policy is LRU across shards per GPU; global capacity enforced via coordinator.
   - Consistency: for model rollback/rollout we version KV keys by model_version + request_id so stale entries don't leak across rollouts.

6) Scheduling and batching
   - Router: tag each request with placement hints (model_version, intended TP/PP layout). Router attempts to send request to nodes that already host pipeline stages to maximize cache hits.
   - Batching: continuous batching within a stage with dynamic batch size up to configured SLO thresholds (max latency, max tokens). For low-latency requests, prefer smaller micro-batches and allocate spare GPUs as "fast path" for critical requests.
   - Preemption: implement soft-preemption where low-priority batches can be deferred in favor of single-request fast-paths. Track preemption fairness to avoid starvation.

NCCL tuning and knobs
---------------------
We need a curated set of NCCL defaults plus per-deployment tuning guides. Initial set of environment variables and patterns to try during experiments:
- NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
- NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0/1 (experiments: disable IB on flaky networks)
- NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 or specific device (for multi-host)
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL or NVL:SYS (controls P2P path choices)
- NCCL_ALGO=RING/HIER (experiment with hierarchical algorithms on large multi-node clusters)
- NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 (for safer runtime failure detection)
- Use NCCL Graph for repeated patterns where supported.

Topology-aware tuning
- Single-host NVLink: enable high-efficiency ring or tree algorithms, ensure P2P enabled.
- Multi-host RDMA (EFA/GPUDirect): prefer hierarchical algorithms that reduce cross-node traffic; tune chunk sizes for reduce-scatter/all-gather to balance latency vs bandwidth.
- Cloud noisy neighbors: surface recommended settings to platform layer and add health checks for NCCL latency spikes.

Empirical experiments (priority list)
----------------------------------
1) Baseline: single-host 4x A100, measure model 13B latency & throughput with no TP/PP.
2) TP-only: 2-way and 4-way TP for 13B and 35B models. Measure per-step latency, all-reduce overhead, and memory usage.
3) TP+PP: 2-stage PP x 2-way TP (total 4 GPUs), micro-batch sizes {1,4,8} to evaluate pipeline bubble tradeoffs.
4) NCCL tuning sweep: test NCCL_ALGO, chunk sizes, P2P settings across single-host and multi-host.
5) KV cache scale test: synthetic workload with many concurrent streams (1000s) to validate memory growth and eviction behavior.
6) Failure injection: simulate GPU/worker loss and validate fallback to non-sharded model or reconfigure placement with minimal request loss.

Metrics to collect
------------------
- P50/P95/P99 per-token latency (end-to-end, and stage-level)
- Tokens/sec per GPU and cluster
- NCCL collective duration distribution (reduce-scatter/all-gather)
- KV cache hit ratio by request and overall memory per GPU
- Recovery time on worker loss and number of affected requests

Failure modes and mitigations
---------------------------
- NCCL hang or slow collectives: detect via timeout and escalate to fallback path (e.g., move request to single-GPU model or alternative region). Track metrics and automatically blacklist problematic nodes.
- GPU OOM during dynamic batching: conservative memory accounting + admission control. If OOM occurs, abort batch and reduce max_batch for that placement.
- Inconsistent KV state after partial failure: use per-request versioning and coordinator-led reconciliation. Avoid cross-request mutation of global KV.

Operational considerations
------------------------
- Model bundles should include placement hints and validated TP/PP configs for common instance types.
- Provide a set of safe defaults for Dedicated and Private customers and an advanced tuning guide for platform operators.
- Rollouts: test model variants in canary with reduced TP/PP degrees before broad rollout.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- What is the best default TP shard layout for common model families (LLM-7B, 13B, 35B, 70B)? Need profiling runs.
- Should we expose an automated placer that picks TP/PP based on target latency/throughput, or keep manual configs only? (Hybrid approach likely).
- How to best minimize cross-stage activation all-gathers? Explore activation compression or quantized transfer.
- Define exact KV eviction and memory-sharing policies for multi-tenant nodes.

Next steps (short-term roadmap)
------------------------------
1) Implement TP-only MVP for 13B model and run basic microbenchmarks (owner: Jordan, collaborator: Ava). Target: 3 weeks.
2) Add KV cache mapping layer to tie KV shards to TP shards and run synthetic gen tests (owner: Priya). Target: 4 weeks.
3) Run NCCL tuning matrix on infra lab (single-host and two-host) and document sweet spots (owner: Kai). Target: 2 weeks after step 1.
4) Integrate basic scheduler hints into router to prefer nodes with warm KV and test end-to-end perf on small cluster (owner: Luis). Target: in-parallel with step 2.

References and links
--------------------
- Megatron-LM TP patterns: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM (notes in CONFLUENCE-RT-45)
- DeepSpeed inference sharding notes: https://www.deepspeed.ai/
- Internal PR #412: initial TP runtime shims (see linked_artifacts).

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This doc is iterating; please add experimental results and any infra-specific tuning notes as comments in-line or link to tickets.
- If you modify placement descriptor format, update model bundle validators and the deployment migration script.
